image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) floating on calm water. The duck features a characteristic iridescent green head, a white neck ring, a grey and brown body, and a yellow bill. One orange webbed foot is visible paddling beneath the water surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, flat, and yellow-green in color, matching the description perfectly.
The eye is visible on the side of the head and appears dark/black, consistent with the taxonomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is streamlined and sits low in the water, indicating buoyancy. The plumage appears dense and smooth, typical of waterproof feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image shows the specific mallard pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, and grey/brown body. This is a full match.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: One leg/foot is visible underwater. It is orange, positioned towards the rear of the body, and clearly shows the webbing between toes. No anatomical errors detected.
The folded wing is visible on the side of the body. While folded, the structure appears consistent with broad, pointed wings tucked against the body. No fusion or melting observed.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is visible at the rear. The characteristic upward curl of the central tail feathers (drake feathers) is clearly present and structurally sound.
